Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 12650 of 2022

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Istekhaf,Pramod Kumar,Satyendra Nath Mishra,Vartika P

Heard Shri Ajay Veer Singh, learned counsel for the accused/applicant, learned A.G.A. for the State

perused the record.
This bail application has been moved by the accused/applicant- Sonu Verma for grant of bail, in
Case Crime No. 374 of 2022, under Sections 376, 504,506 Ipc & Section 3/4 of the Protection of
Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and Section 67-C of I.T. Act, Police Station Kotwali Dehat,
District Sultanpur, during trial.

sentences.text:
It is further submitted that the FIR of this case has been lodged by moving an application U/s 156(3)
CrPC.
The allegation of committing sexual intercourse on the basis of false promise of marriage has been levelled in the FIR as well as in the statement of the prosecutrix recorded U/s 161 & 164 CrPC.

However, during the course of the trial, the statement of the prosecutrix U/s 161 & 164 CrPC as well as of her mother (informant) has been recorded by the trial court as PW-1 and PW-2 and both these witnesses have turned hostile and have not supported the version of the prosecution.

It is further submitted that the age of the prosecutrix, as per her educational credential, was 15 years and 9 months on the date and time of the alleged incident while as per ossification age, her bone age has been determined as 17 years.
Having regard to the aforesaid, the prosecutrix appears to be major on the date and time of the alleged incident and she was having sufficient intellect to understand her welfare.
It is further submitted that the applicant is in jail in this case since 1.9.2022 and he is not having any criminal antecedents.
Charge sheet in the matter has already been filed and there is no apprehension that the accused-applicant after release on bail, may flee from the process of law or may otherwise misuse the liberty.
Learned A.G.A., on the other hand submits that having manner on which the offence has been committed the applicant is not entitled for any relief.

Learned counsel appearing for the opposite party no.2 fairly submits that the prosecutrix as well as the informant has chosen not to support the version of the prosecution before the trial court and he is having instructions not to oppose the bail application of the applicant.

Having heard learned counsel for the parties and having perused the record, it is reflected that educational age of the prosecutrix is about 15 years and 9 months and as per ossification test, her age is coming about 17 years on the date and time of the alleged incident.
The prosecutrix in her statement before the trial court has not supported the version of the prosecution and stated that no sexual intercourse took place with her.
Similar is the condition of the informant.

On this basis, it is vehemently submitted on behalf of the applicant that the prosecution would not able to secure conviction of the applicant before the trial court as the informant and victim have chosen not to support the case of the prosecution before the trial court.
The applicant is in jail in this case since 1.9.2022 without any criminal history.
Charge sheet in the matter has already been filed.
His presence could be secured before the trial court by placing any adequate conditions.

Keeping in view the nature of the offence, evidence, complicity of the accused, severity of punishment, submissions of the learned counsel for the parties and without expressing any opinion on the merits and demerits of the case, I am of the considered view that applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

Let the applicant- Sonu Verma involved in the aforesaid case be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond with two sureties in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions:-
Sonu Verma vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko ... on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111901093/
2 (i) The applicant shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence by intimidating/pressurizing the witnesses, during the investigation or trial.
(ii) The applicant shall cooperate in the trial sincerely without seeking any adjournment.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal activity or commission of any crime after being released on bail.
